card.architecture: Mage-Flow-Edit 4B native-resolution MMDiT (Mage-VAE + Qwen3-VL-4B encoder, rectified flow), RL-aligned
card.summary: Microsoft's 4B instruction-based image editor. Background replacement, style/lighting changes, localized content edits, restoration, and multi-reference editing (1-3 refs). RL-aligned with full CFG; ~30 steps. Output follows the source size (native 512-2048).
card.pick_when: Instruction editing on a compact model with real CFG control and optional reference images.

prompt.guidance: State what to KEEP, then what to CHANGE, in natural language (English recommended). Refer to attachments as 'the reference image'. RL-aligned: guidance ~5, ~30 steps.
prompt.example: Keep the woman, her pose and dress unchanged. Replace the background with a wide, flat grassland prairie under soft golden sunlight, open sky, endless green fields.
prompt.overview: A unified image+text editor (Qwen3-VL): the instruction and the reference image(s) are encoded together, and reference content is aligned to the output by position. Output size follows the (resized ~1MP) reference by default.
prompt.instructions: Write the instruction as: what to keep, then what to change. English recommended. Attach 1-3 reference images and name what to take from each ('the reference image'). RL-aligned, so it responds to guidance_scale ~5 and negative prompts; ~30 steps. References are resized to the output resolution before encoding.
do: Say what to keep, then what to change
Name what to take from each reference
prompt.negative_guidance: Supported (true CFG at guidance ~5) -- leave empty by default; populate to suppress artifacts.

ui_help.note: Say what to keep, then what to change -- like giving directions to an editor. Attach the picture(s) to work from.
ui_help.good_for: instruction edits: backgrounds, style, add/remove, restoration

edit_use_cases: instruction image editing (background replace, style/lighting, add/remove/recolour, restoration); 1-3 reference images

reference.hint: Describe the change and refer to an attached picture as 'the reference image'. Name what to take from it (e.g. 'use the jacket from the reference image; keep her face'). You can attach up to three references.
